userText:
Building: Gare de Lyon, Paris (railway station).
The front (−z) is the station front on the Place Louis-Armand.
Footprint: 180.9 m along x by 221.1 m along z, centred on the origin.
Outline (approximate: the hull of its OpenStreetMap parts), [x, z] in metres, going round:
[[-90.1,106.6],[-90.4,85.6],[-86.6,47],[-25.2,-81.7],[-5.9,-101.9],[1.2,-106],[89.1,-110.5],[90.4,-91.8],[90.4,109.4],[6,110.5]]
Height: the highest point is 67 m above the ground.

3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. front three-quarter from the forecourt: long Beaux-Arts facade with arches, mansard roofs and the tall clock tower, daylight
  2. high view looking down along the station's train shed roofs and tracks
  3. view of the long arcaded facade and mansard roof from the other end, tower out of frame, daylight

Reply with the JSON object only.

json.notes: A long cream Beaux-Arts station front along the -z side, with a round-arched ground arcade, pilasters and a dormered slate mansard, and a tall square clock tower with a dome at the +x end. Behind it, long barrel-vault glazed train sheds run back along the tracks, and a tall flat-roofed office block stands on the +x side. The clock tower and the arcaded front are the signature features.

photos: photo 1: the station front from the forecourt, south-west side. A long cream Beaux-Arts facade with a tall arched ground floor, a mansard roof with dormers, and the square clock tower on the right (+x) end with a dome and lantern.
photo 2: high aerial view along the train-shed roofs. Long barrel-shaped glazed roofs run away from the front over the tracks, with office blocks on the right (+x) side.

photo 3: the arcaded facade from the other end, tower out of frame. Round-headed arches over a shallow ground arcade, pilasters between windows, and a steep mansard with dormers and sculpture on the roofline.
